title: Special Suits Could Make Japan's Castles More Accessible
paragraphs: Japan's old castles are popular with tourists, but they can be very hard to visit for people who use wheelchairs. Many castles have steep stone steps and hills. Now, one city in Japan is testing a new way to help, using special suits.

The test took place on October 19, 2026, at Hikone Castle in Shiga Prefecture, near Lake Biwa. Hikone Castle is one of only 12 castles in Japan that still have their original main tower. To reach the top area of the castle, visitors must climb 140 steep stone steps. The steps were built hundreds of years ago to make it hard for enemies to attack.

Hikone city does not want to build concrete ramps over the old stone walls. So, city workers and volunteers tested another idea. They carried people in wheelchairs up to the castle in a yamakago, a traditional wooden seat that is carried by people. In Japan's past, important people were often carried in this way.

The route was 285 meters long, there and back, and it went up 50 meters. There were six carriers, and they all wore special suits to support their backs and legs. These suits do not use motors. Instead, they make it easier to stand up and carry heavy loads. When people carry a yamakago, it can pull them backward as they stand up. The suits made this smoother and safer.

The carriers liked the suits. One carrier, who had hurt their lower back in the past, said that the suit made them feel safe. Another said that they only noticed how much the suit had helped after taking it off.

In the future, guides could explain the history of the castle during the trip, so visitors can feel like important people from the time of the samurai. The idea could also help make other castles, temples and historic places in Japan easier to visit.
